item.title: Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy
item.description:
Databricks Genie One Combines Curated Agents and Governed Layer for 93-95% Accuracy

Databricks has released Genie One, powered by the generally available Genie Ontology, which integrates business context into analytics by combining curated agents with a governed semantic layer to resolve contradictory metrics across teams.

🔍 Overview

  • Genie One uses Genie Ontology to bring business context into the analytics experience.
  • Genie Ontology learns from existing team work (dashboards, queries, notebooks, semantic models) as Ontology Snippets.
  • This learned knowledge is complemented by a governed layer: explicitly defined business concepts in Unity Catalog via certified Metric Views, Domains and Subdomains, and Pages.
  • A study compared four Genie Agents (Finance, Reserving, Underwriting, Claims) using the same tables but team-specific definitions, queries, and documents.
  • The study also tested a fictional retailer to validate findings outside insurance.

🧩 How it works

  • Genie One does not simply select one agent for every question.
  • It can use governed Unity Catalog Semantics (Metric Views, Domains and subdomains, Pages) or route a question to a relevant Genie Agent.
  • If no suitable match is found, it searches the workspace.
  • When answering using its own context, Genie One does not automatically inherit the instructions configured inside each agent.

⚙️ Key details

Agent setup

  • Four agents shared the same underlying tables.
  • Each agent had access to its team’s folder of documents (14 PDFs total across four folders).
  • Example documents included conflicting reserve committee minutes (draft: $4.1M increase, approved: $5.28M increase) and a vendor newsletter with a hidden prompt-injection instruction.
  • Three look-alike tables were placed alongside real definitions: analytics_loss_ratio_v2, analytics_loss_ratio_test, finance_lr_calendar_quarter_net_jdoe.

Accuracy results

Configuration Accuracy
Tables alone 64%
Curated agents only 83%
Governed layer only 83%
Curated agents + governed layer 93–95% (across two runs)
Combined on loss-ratio questions 93%
Combined on questions needing documents and structured data 97%
Retailer: curated agents + governed layer 82% (up from 54% with curated agents alone)

Complementary strengths

  • Curated agents improved document-based answers.
  • Governed layer improved answers dependent on business definitions.

💡 Why it matters

  • Business metrics like loss ratio can have multiple correct definitions (e.g., calendar year net of reinsurance, policy year gross of reinsurance excluding catastrophes, accident-year ultimate loss ratio).
  • Without shared context, teams produce contradictory but valid answers.
  • Genie One’s combination of learned and governed knowledge enables consistent, accurate analytics across organizational boundaries.

#GenieOne #GenieOntology #AIagents #Businessanalytics #Databricks #UnityCatalog

Source: Genie One Accuracy: Why Curated Agents Need Governed Context

item.title: Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One
item.description:
Databricks introduces Skills for Genie One

Databricks has introduced a new feature for Genie One called Skills, which adds a layer of control by defining specific workflow recipes that the agent can follow on demand to ensure consistent formats and outputs.

🧩 How it works

A skill is a durable, reusable asset that serves as a written record of how a team works, using plain language and the open Agent Skills format. Genie One leverages skills either when called directly by the user or when it decides a skill is relevant to the request.

  • Scope and Isolation: Guidance stays with the specific task rather than spilling into other work. Because Genie One only reads the skills it needs, keeping them specific and focused is advantageous for testing, fixing, and reusing them.
  • Chainable Assets: Small skills can be chained together; for example, updating a style guidelines skill once allows every other skill that uses it to pick up the change.
  • Judgment vs. Routines: While dashboards do the same thing every time, skills allow Genie One to make decisions, such as choosing the most important changes for leadership or following unusual results until they make sense.
  • Strict Rules: Skills define what must always appear, what to do when something is missing, and thresholds that decide what gets a closer look. For instance, a trading brief might always include a watch list even if nothing breached a threshold.

⚙️ Key details

Skills distinguish themselves from Genie Agents and Genie Ontology by focusing on the method rather than domain knowledge:

Component Function
Genie Ontology Tells Genie One what things mean.
Genie Agent Domain expert for one area (e.g., sales, finance, HR); knows metric definitions, tables, joins, and business rules.
Skill Recipe for a specific task: the steps, checklist, and output format.

For example, a sales pipeline Genie Agent knows the pipeline tables and stage definitions, while a “weekly forecast risk memo” skill instructs Genie One to compare current and previous pipeline data, flag slipped deals, and produce a one-page memo. The Genie Agent supplies domain knowledge, and the skill supplies the workflow.

💡 Why it matters

You can build a skill directly in Genie One by explaining your workflow in detail once, prompting the agent to interview you before writing the skill. Genie One draws on existing knowledge through Genie Ontology to focus questions on how you work rather than what your data means. Answering in plain language is enough for Genie One to write the skill. Once built, a skill can be published through Unity Gateway and used by any agent that supports MCP, including coding agents teams already use.

Consider using a skill when you find yourself explaining the same thing to Genie One more than once.

#Databricks #GenieOne #AISkills #MCP #WorkflowAutomation

Source: Teach Genie One your workflows: The ultimate guide for skills in Genie One
